issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (returns the total number of students). The solution implementation instead defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) with a boolean parameter. This parameter mismatch deviates from the specified signature and will confuse students about which method to implement and how to compute the total (with or without guests). It also likely causes test or compatibility failures if automated tests expect the no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution conform to the specification by providing a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (inscribed + guest). If optional behavior is desired, add an overloaded method (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)) in addition to the required no-arg method, but do not replace the specified signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the method signature for the same conceptual operation (obtaining the total number of students) and can confuse students mapping the task requirements to the provided/expected implementation. Tests and instructions expect a no-arg method; introducing a boolean parameter is an unintended naming/signature inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the no-argument signature expected by the problem/UML by implementing getTotalNumberOfStudents() : int. If conditional inclusion of guest students is desired, add an overloaded method getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) that delegates to the no-arg version or vice versa, but keep the no-arg method present to match the specification.
